text: – LLNL-TR-2013901 2 Executive Summary The data center market is poised to explode in the coming decade due to undeniable drivers such as continued adoption of generative AI, increased data storage needs, and enterprise integration of AI in numerous industries [1] [2] [3]. Scalable power and increased computational capacity are at the forefront of considerations for hyperscalers, the major cloud service providers in this space. Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory is uniquely poised to help with informed decision making for data center market leaders during this phase of explosive expansion. National grid modeling expertise and cutting- edge innovations in computer cooling systems place LLNL in an enviable position for creating economic impact in the data center industry by leveraging its expertise in these areas which can help the data center market keep up with growing demand. The government has identified increasing data centers in the United States as an issue of importance and continues to back the growth of this largely US based market. A path forward, including collaborations where industry leverages national lab expertise, supports a promising future for data centers and Lawrence Livermore National Laboratory. Data Center Market Report – LLNL-TR-2013901 3 Data Center Market Overview: Landscape, Segmentation, and Strategic Investments Market Background The global data center market is experiencing rapid growth, driven by soaring demand for computing power fueled by generative AI, the expansion of cloud computing, and increasing data storage needs [1] [3] [2]. Valued at $347.60 billion in 2024, the market is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of 11.2% through 2030 [4]. North America held the largest share of the market in 2024 and is expected to maintain its dominance in the near term [1] [4], supported by significant investments from major cloud service providers, known as hyperscalers. Industry leaders such as Meta, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services are scaling their infrastructure to meet rising demands, with an estimated $1.8 trillion in capital expenditures required between 2024 and 2030 [5]. Worldwide an investment of $6.7 trillion in data centers is expected to be required to keep pace with demand by 2030 [1]. As the backbone of modern digital infrastructure, the data center market is poised to play a critical role in shaping the future of compute technology and market opportunities. Key Players The data center market is highly competitive with multiple key players driving the market growth despite the high upfront costs required to enter the industry. Market leaders such as Meta, Google, Microsoft, and Amazon Web Services dominate the space by offering large-scale cloud service solutions and are investing heavily in expanding their infrastructure [4] [5] [6]. These hyperscalers are building new data centers with enhanced power capacities to meet the growing demand for computing and storage. Other notable players include Alibaba Cloud in China, which is rapidly expanding its presence in Asia, and U.S.-based companies Dell and Equinix, Inc. [4]. As the market continues to evolve, these market leaders are shaping the future of global digital infrastructure through innovation and strategic investments.
